Indoor window treatments

Plantation Shutters in Palm Beach County

A finished, built-in look with louvers you can tilt for light and privacy. Each shutter is made to fit its window.

Get a Free Consultation Call 561-332-8091

We bring samples to your home so you can compare options at your own windows.

Is it a fit?

Where plantation shutters work well

  • Rooms where you want a permanent, architectural look
  • Privacy with adjustable light through the day
  • Bathrooms and kitchens, with moisture-resistant materials
  • Homeowners who want something durable and easy to wipe clean
Ask about plantation shutters

Good to know before you choose

Material
Wood and composite are the common choices. Composite generally handles humidity better, which matters in bathrooms and Florida homes.
Louver size
Larger louvers give a more open view when tilted. Smaller louvers suit smaller windows and a more traditional look.
Doors and sliders
Sliding doors usually need bypass or bifold panels, which depend on the space beside the door. We'll check this when we measure.
How it works

Three steps to finished plantation shutters

  1. Consultation at your home

    We bring samples, look at your windows in real light, and talk through what you need.

  2. Measurement and a written proposal

    Each opening is measured, and you get the products, options, and price in writing.

  3. Installation and walkthrough

    Our own installers fit, adjust, and explain everything before they leave.

Questions

Plantation Shutters questions

How are shutters different from blinds?

Shutters are a fixed frame with hinged panels, so they read as part of the room. Blinds raise and lower. Shutters stay in place and you tilt the louvers or swing the panels open.

Do shutters block all light?

Closed shutters block most light, but small amounts can pass around the louvers and panel edges. For a very dark bedroom, we may suggest pairing them with drapery.

How long do custom shutters take?

Shutters are made to order, so there's a production period before installation. We'll give you the expected timing in your proposal.
